task.title: Font variants and features
task.shortdesc: Fonts can contain alternate letter shapes, number styles and ligatures. Use the properties in this guide to request those forms. The result depends on the selected font and its font-synthesis settings. See Font selection and sizing for the synthesis properties and their values.

info.p: CSS Fonts 4 §6.3, Kerning: the font-kerning property.
Kerning adjusts the space between particular pairs of letters when the font provides kerning data. Use normal to request kerning, none to turn it off, or auto to let the processor decide.
CSS Fonts 4 §6.4, Ligatures: the font-variant-ligatures property.
Ligatures replace certain letter combinations with a single designed glyph. Use this property to control common, discretionary, historical or contextual ligatures.

stepxmp.pre: body { font-variant-ligatures: common-ligatures; } code { font-variant-ligatures: none; }

info.p: normal uses the default feature behavior. For OpenType fonts, common ligatures and contextual forms are on by default. Discretionary and historical ligatures are off by default. none disables all kinds of ligatures and contextual forms covered by this property.

ul.li: common-ligatures enables common ligatures, such as fi or fl, when the font provides them. no-common-ligatures disables them.
discretionary-ligatures enables optional ligatures intended for particular styles. no-discretionary-ligatures disables them.
historical-ligatures enables historical ligatures. no-historical-ligatures disables them.
contextual enables contextual forms, where a glyph changes according to nearby characters. no-contextual disables them.

info.p: You can combine one value from each pair. Required ligatures used to render complex scripts are not affected by these settings.
CSS Fonts 4 §6.6, Capitalization: the font-variant-caps property.
Use font-variant-caps to request small capitals or other capitalization forms from a font.

normal uses the usual letter forms. small-caps uses small capitals for lowercase letters. all-small-caps uses small capitals for both lowercase and uppercase letters. petite-caps uses petite capitals for lowercase letters. all-petite-caps uses petite capitals for both cases. unicase uses small capitals for uppercase letters with ordinary lowercase letters. titling-caps requests capitals designed for titles.
If the font does not provide the requested forms, font-synthesis-small-caps determines whether the processor synthesizes them.
CSS Fonts 4 §6.5, Subscript and superscript forms: the font-variant-position property.
Use font-variant-position to request subscript or superscript glyph forms from the font.

normal uses the ordinary glyphs. sub requests subscript glyphs. super requests superscript glyphs. The alternate glyphs use the same em-box and baseline as ordinary glyphs, so this property does not resize or reposition them. It does not change the meaning or position of the XML element. If the font does not provide the requested forms, font-synthesis-position determines whether the processor synthesizes them.
CSS Fonts 4 §6.7, Numerical formatting: the font-variant-numeric property.
Use this property to request number shapes, spacing and fractions. normal uses the font’s default forms. You may combine one value from each mutually exclusive pair:

ul.li: lining-nums requests figures aligned with the capital-letter height. oldstyle-nums requests figures with ascenders and descenders.
proportional-nums requests figures whose widths vary. tabular-nums requests figures with equal widths.
diagonal-fractions requests a numerator and denominator separated by a diagonal slash. stacked-fractions requests a numerator above a denominator.
ordinal requests letter forms used with ordinal numbers, such as the suffix in 1st. slashed-zero requests a zero glyph with a slash.

info.p: The font must provide each requested feature.
CSS Fonts 4 §6.8, Alternates and swashes: the font-variant-alternates property.
Use normal to request no named alternate. Otherwise, combine one or more alternate requests:

stylistic(name) requests one named stylistic alternate. historical-forms requests historical glyph forms. styleset(name, ...) requests one or more named stylistic sets. character-variant(name, ...) requests named variants for individual characters. swash(name) requests a named swash form. ornaments(name) requests a named ornament. annotation(name) requests a named annotation form.

Names in these functions are case-sensitive. A name can be defined for a font family by @font-feature-values. If it is not defined for the selected family and feature type, it has no effect. The font must support the mapped feature.
CSS Fonts 4 §6.9, Defining font specific alternates: the @font-feature-values rule.

Use @font-feature-values to give readable names to alternate features that a font identifies by OpenType feature tags. Its prelude is one or more named font families separated by commas. Generic and system font names are not allowed. Inside the block, use feature-value rules to map names to the font-specific integer indexes.
CSS Fonts 4 §6.9.1, Basic syntax.
Each nested rule has a declaration block. A declaration maps a case-sensitive name to a non-negative integer or integer list. The meaning and number of integers depend on the rule:

ul.li: @stylistic maps a name to one stylistic-alternate index for OpenType feature salt.
@historical-forms maps a name to one or more historical-form indexes for OpenType feature hist.

@styleset maps a name to one or more style-set indexes. Values from 1 through 99 select the corresponding ss01 through ss99 features. The OpenType standard defines ss01 through ss20; later feature tags may be used by fonts that support them. The value 0 and values above 99 are syntactically valid but enable no OpenType feature. See CSS Fonts 4 §6.9.2.

@character-variant maps a name to one or two indexes. The first selects cv01 through cv99; the optional second sets that feature’s variant value. A first index of 0 or greater than 99 is valid but enables no feature. See CSS Fonts 4 §6.9.2.
@swash maps a name to one swash index for OpenType feature swsh or cswh.
@ornaments maps a name to one ornament index for OpenType feature ornm.
@annotation maps a name to one annotation index for OpenType feature nalt.

info.p: Repeated feature-value rules of the same type contribute their declarations together. If the same family, rule type and name are defined more than once, the last definition is used.

@font-feature-values also accepts a font-display descriptor. Its initial value is auto , which leaves the policy to the processor. The descriptor sets the default font-display policy for @font-face rules for the listed family when those rules do not set their own font-display. block uses a short block period, with 3 seconds recommended, followed by an infinite swap period. swap uses an extremely short block period, with 100 milliseconds or less recommended, followed by an infinite swap period. fallback uses an extremely short block period, with 100 milliseconds or less recommended, followed by a short swap period, with 3 seconds recommended. optional uses the font only if it is available for the first rendering. Otherwise, the block and swap periods are treated as expired, so the fallback remains in use.
CSS Fonts 4 §6.10, East Asian text rendering: the font-variant-east-asian property.
Use normal to request none of the variants below. You can combine a glyph-variant value, a width value and ruby:

ul.li: jis78 , jis83 , jis90 and jis04 request Japanese glyph forms from the corresponding JIS standard editions.
simplified requests simplified-character forms. traditional requests traditional-character forms.
full-width requests full-width glyphs. proportional-width requests proportionally spaced glyphs.
ruby requests glyph forms designed for ruby text.

info.p: The font must provide the requested forms. Ruby-specific glyphs are designed to remain legible at the smaller sizes used for ruby text.
CSS Fonts 4 §6.13, Font language override: the font-language-override property.

Set the text’s language with a BCP 47 tag in xml:lang. For example, tr identifies Turkish and en-GB identifies British English. Use a language tag that follows BCP 47 and its registered subtags in the IANA Language Subtag Registry.

Fonts can use OpenType language-system tags to select language-specific glyph features. Normally, the text’s BCP 47 language lets the processor choose the corresponding OpenType system. Set font-language-override only when you need to select a different OpenType system, such as when the font lacks the system for the text’s language.

For example, use xml:lang="mk" to identify Macedonian text. If the selected font lacks a Macedonian language system but provides Serbian conventions that suit the text, "SRB" selects its Serbian OpenType system.

normal uses the OpenType system inferred from the text’s BCP 47 language. A string must be a case-sensitive OpenType language-system tag, not a BCP 47 tag. Find the tag in the font’s documentation or in Microsoft’s OpenType language system tags. The tag is matched as four characters; shorter strings are padded at the end with U+0020 spaces. Unknown tags are ignored. Leave the value as normal unless you need to override the inferred system.
CSS Fonts 4 §9.3, Selecting the text presentation style: The font-variant-emoji property.

normal lets the processor choose text or emoji presentation according to its usual policy. text treats each character that can have emoji presentation as if followed by U+FE0E, the text presentation selector. emoji treats each such character as if followed by U+FE0F, the emoji presentation selector. unicode follows the Unicode default presentation for each character. An explicit text or emoji variation selector in the text overrides that default.
The selected font must contain the requested glyphs and presentation.
CSS Fonts 4 §6.11, Overall shorthand for font rendering: the font-variant property.

Use font-variant to set several variant properties in one declaration. normal resets every subproperty to its initial value. none sets font-variant-ligatures to none and resets the other variant subproperties. Otherwise, combine compatible values from the ligature, capitalization, alternate, numeric, East Asian, position and emoji groups described above. Omitted subproperties reset to their initial values.

stepxmp.pre: body { font-variant: small-caps; } table { font-variant: lining-nums tabular-nums; }

info.p: Use a longhand such as font-variant-numeric when you want to control only one kind of feature. The font shorthand is different. It resets font variant settings rather than setting all these detailed choices. font-variant does not reset font-language-override, font-feature-settings or font-variation-settings.
CSS Fonts 4 §6.12, Low-level font feature settings control: the font-feature-settings property.
Use font-feature-settings to set a specific OpenType feature directly. Write the feature tag as a four-character string, followed by an optional number, on or off.

normal makes no change to glyph selection or positioning. Otherwise, give one or more comma-separated <feature-tag-value> items. Each tag is a case-sensitive string of four printable ASCII characters, from U+0020 through U+007E. The font must define the tag. Unsupported tags are ignored. This property does not synthesize their behavior, except that a processor may synthesize kerning for fonts with a legacy kern table.

For each tag, omit the value or use on to enable the feature with value 1. Use off or 0 to disable it. The optional integer value cannot be negative. A positive integer enables the feature and selects its indexed form when it has multiple forms. on is equivalent to 1; off is equivalent to 0. If a tag is repeated, its last value takes precedence.
In the example, liga is the standard ligature feature and 0 disables it. Prefer a higher-level property such as font-variant-ligatures when it describes the feature you need.
